claim: Legionella pneumophila recruits many Rab GTPases to its vacuole and exploits their activities.
source: Legionella pneumophila recruits many Rab GTPases to its vacuole and exploits their activities.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about L. pneumophila infection.

claim: Phosphoribosyl-ubiquitination of Rab10 catalyzed by the SidE ligases is crucial for its recruitment to the bacterial vacuole.
source: Phosphoribosyl-ubiquitination of Rab10 catalyzed by the SidE ligases is crucial for its recruitment to the bacterial vacuole.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: SdcB resides on the vacuole and contributes to retention of Rab10 at the late stages of infection.
source: SdcB, the previously uncharacterized SidC-family effector, resides on the vacuole and contributes to retention of Rab10 at the late stages of infection.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: MavC is a negative regulator of SdcB.
source: We further identified MavC as a negative regulator of SdcB.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 5-7.

claim: MavC crosslinks ubiquitin to SdcB by transglutaminase activity and suppresses its function.
source: By the transglutaminase activity, MavC crosslinks ubiquitin to SdcB and suppresses its function, resulting in elimination of Rab10 from the vacuole.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: MavC-mediated suppression of SdcB results in elimination of Rab10 from the vacuole.
source: By the transglutaminase activity, MavC crosslinks ubiquitin to SdcB and suppresses its function, resulting in elimination of Rab10 from the vacuole.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: Legionella pneumophila utilizes a large arsenal of effector proteins delivered via its Dot/Icm type IV secretion system to modulate host cellular systems.
source: Legionella pneumophila utilizes a large arsenal of effector proteins which are delivered via its Dot/Icm type IV secretion system (T4SS) to modulate host cellular systems (Hubber and Roy, 2010; Kubori and Nagai, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The functions of effector proteins are crucial for establishing a replicative niche where L. pneumophila can survive and avoid host defense mechanisms.
source: The functions of the effector proteins are crucial for establishing a replicative niche where L. pneumophila can survive and avoid host defense mechanisms in the cell (Isberg et al., 2009; Qiu and Luo, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Many effector proteins modulate the function of host Rab GTPases that regulate cellular membrane transport.
source: Many effector proteins are known to modulate the function of host Rab GTPases that regulates cellular membrane transport (Neunuebel and Machner, 2012; Sherwood and Roy, 2013; Spanò and Galán, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Effector manipulation of Rab1 has been extensively analyzed in L. pneumophila infection.
source: Among them, effector manipulation of Rab1, a critical regulator of membrane trafficking between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the Golgi complex, has been extensively analyzed in L. pneumophila infection (Arasaki et al., 2012; Ingmundson et al., 2007; Machner and Isberg, 2006; Mukherjee et al., 2011; Müller et al., 2010; Murata et al., 2006; Neunuebel et al., 2011; Tan and Luo, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Ubiquitination regulates all aspects of eukaryotic cell physiology and is exploited by various bacterial pathogens.
source: Ubiquitination regulates all aspects of eukaryotic cell physiology, and therefore is exploited by various bacterial pathogens encoding ubiquitin (Ub) ligases and deubiquitinases (DUBs) (Ashida and Sasakawa, 2017; Kitao et al., 2020; Kubori et al., 2019; Lin and Machner, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SidC and SdcA are Legionella E3 ligases that mediate ubiquitin modification of Rab1.
source: Effector-mediated Ub modification of Rab1 was reported as an action of the Legionella E3 ligase SidC and its paralog SdcA (Horenkamp et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab33b, Rab1, Rab6A, and Rab30 are conjugated with phosphoribosylated (PR)-Ub by the SidE family of effector proteins.
source: Rab33b as well as Rab1, Rab6A, and Rab30 are conjugated with phosphoribosylated (PR)-Ub by the unique reaction mechanism of the SidE family of effector proteins (Qiu et al., 2016), and it was shown that recruitment of Rab33b and Rab6A to the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) relies on the PR ubiquitination of Rab33b (Kawabata et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Recruitment of Rab33b and Rab6A to the LCV relies on PR ubiquitination of Rab33b.
source: Rab33b as well as Rab1, Rab6A, and Rab30 are conjugated with phosphoribosylated (PR)-Ub by the unique reaction mechanism of the SidE family of effector proteins (Qiu et al., 2016), and it was shown that recruitment of Rab33b and Rab6A to the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) relies on the PR ubiquitination of Rab33b (Kawabata et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 is required for optimal intracellular replication of L. pneumophila.
source: A recent genome-wide screen identified host factors including Rab10 linked to intracellular replication of L. pneumophila (Jeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 is recruited to the LCV and is ubiquitinated depending on the activity of SidC and SdcA.
source: It was demonstrated that Rab10 is recruited to the LCV and is ubiquitinated depending on the activity of SidC and SdcA (Jeng et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SidC and SdcA were originally identified as tethering factors that function in ER-to-LCV trafficking.
source: SidC and SdcA were originally identified as tethering factors that function in ER-to-LCV trafficking both having a unique phosphatidylinositol-4 phosphate (PI[4]P)-binding domain (Ragaz et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The enzymatic activity of SidC and SdcA as Ub ligases is encoded in the SNL domain.
source: The enzymatic activity was found to be encoded in the domain conserved between the two proteins, namely SidC N-terminal Ub ligase (SNL) domain (Hsu et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SdcB (Lpg2452/LegA14) was identified as another L. pneumophila Ub ligase having the SNL domain.
source: SdcB (Lpg2452/LegA14) was identified as another L. pneumophila Ub ligase having the SNL domain (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The role of SdcB in L. pneumophila infection has not been examined prior to this study.
source: However, the role of SdcB in L. pneumophila infection has not been examined yet.
evidence: This statement indicates a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: MavC chemically modifies the E2 enzyme UBE2N by catalyzing a covalent linkage between Ub and UBE2N.
source: They are exemplified by MavC which was shown to chemically modify the E2 enzyme UBE2N. The transglutaminase activity of MavC catalyzes a covalent linkage between Ub and UBE2N, thereby abolishing the activity of UBE2N to form polyUb chains, and mediate host NFκB signaling (Gan et al., 2019a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MavC abolishes the activity of UBE2N to form polyUb chains and mediate host NFκB signaling.
source: The transglutaminase activity of MavC catalyzes a covalent linkage between Ub and UBE2N, thereby abolishing the activity of UBE2N to form polyUb chains, and mediate host NFκB signaling (Gan et al., 2019a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MvcA is a paralog of MavC and exhibits similar activity to MavC as a Ub-specific deamidase.
source: Encoded by the neighboring gene of mavC, MvcA is a paralog of MavC and exhibits similar activity to MavC as a Ub-specific deamidase (Valleau et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MvcA can reverse MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to UBE2N by its unique DUB activity.
source: However, MvcA was found to have an ability to reverse MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to UBE2N by its unique DUB activity (Gan et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The enzymatic activities of MavC and MvcA are both inhibited by Lpg2149.
source: The enzymatic activities of MavC and MvcA are both inhibited by Lpg2149, an effector encoded downstream of mvcA, by blocking their catalytic residues (Valleau et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Upon infection with wild-type L. pneumophila for 1 hr, Rab10 was detected with a shifted band of higher molecular mass containing Ub.
source: Upon infection of HEK293T-FcγRII cells transiently expressing FLAG-Rab10 and HA-Ub with a wild-type L. pneumophila strain (Lp01) for 1 hr, Rab10 was detected with a shifted band of higher molecular mass (Figure 1a, upper panel). The band was shown to contain Ub by probing with an anti-HA antibody (Figure 1a, lower panel), indicating that the band represents Rab10 conjugated with a single Ub molecule.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Rab10 can be monoubiquitinated in a T4SS-dependent manner.
source: The mass shift was not detected in cells infected with the T4SS-deficient strain (ΔdotA), suggesting that Rab10 can be monoubiquitinated in a T4SS-dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing wild-type and ΔdotA strains in Figure 1a.

claim: Infection with a ΔsidEs strain mostly eliminated the molecular mass shift of Rab10.
source: Infection with a ΔsidEs strain lacking all four SidE-family proteins (SidE, SdeA, SdeB, and SdeC) mostly eliminated the molecular mass shift of Rab10, while infection with a strain lacking the negative regulators of SidE-family proteins (DupA, DupB, SidJ, and SdjA; Black et al., 2019; Gan et al., 2019b; Qiu et al., 2017; Shin et al., 2020; Sulpizio et al., 2019) enhanced the intensity of the band (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Infection with a strain lacking negative regulators of SidE-family proteins enhanced the intensity of the monoubiquitinated Rab10 band.
source: Infection with a ΔsidEs strain lacking all four SidE-family proteins (SidE, SdeA, SdeB, and SdeC) mostly eliminated the molecular mass shift of Rab10, while infection with a strain lacking the negative regulators of SidE-family proteins (DupA, DupB, SidJ, and SdjA; Black et al., 2019; Gan et al., 2019b; Qiu et al., 2017; Shin et al., 2020; Sulpizio et al., 2019) enhanced the intensity of the band (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a and citations to previous literature.

claim: The SidE-family proteins can conjugate PR-Ub to Rab10.
source: These results suggest that the SidE-family proteins can conjugate PR-Ub to Rab10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Polyubiquitination of Rab10 is linked with its PR ubiquitination.
source: The high molecular weight smears detected with anti-HA antibody are thought to be polyUb chains (Figure 1a, lower panel). Appearance of these smears is tightly associated with the PR-Ub bands, showing that polyubiquitination of Rab10 is linked with its PR ubiquitination.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: PR-Ub conjugation to Rab10 can enhance its modification with polyUb chains.
source: To examine if PR-Ub conjugation to Rab10 can enhance its modification with polyUb chains, we infected HEK293T-FcγRII cells expressing FLAG-Rab10 and HA-Ub with the ΔsidEs strain complemented with a plasmid expressing wild-type or a catalytic mutant of SdeA (SdeAEE/AA), a representative SidE-family protein (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: SdeA strongly enhanced polyUb smear in a manner depending on its mono-ADP ribosyltransferase activity.
source: We detected a strongly enhanced polyUb smear whose appearance depends on the mono-ADP ribosyltransferase activity of SdeA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b comparing wild-type and catalytic mutant SdeA.

claim: The intensity of monoubiquitination band was correlated with that of the polyUb smears.
source: The intensity of the monoubiquitination band was correlated with that of the polyUb smears (Figure 1b, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: When the C-terminal GG motif of Ub was replaced with AA, the polyUb smear drastically diminished.
source: When the C-terminal GG motif of Ub was replaced with AA (UbAA), the polyUb smear drastically diminished, and accumulation of monoUb-conjugated Rab10 was observed instead.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The polyUb chains on Rab10 were formed via the Ub C-terminus by the canonical ubiquitination reaction.
source: This indicates that the polyUb chains on Rab10 were formed via the Ub C-terminus by the canonical ubiquitination reaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with UbAA shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The observed monoUb conjugation to Rab10 does not require the Ub C-terminus.
source: This also shows that the observed monoUb conjugation to Rab10 does not require the Ub C-terminus, which is consistent with the formation of bridge between Arg42 of Ub and substrate catalyzed by the SidE effectors (Bhogaraju et al., 2016; Kotewicz et al., 2017; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with UbAA shown in Figure 1b, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 is subjected to SdeA-mediated PR ubiquitination.
source: These results strongly support that Rab10 is subjected to SdeA-mediated PR ubiquitination and that this modification may provide a platform of conjugation of polyUb chains to Rab10, which is expected to be mediated by other Ub ligases.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: PR ubiquitination of Rab10 may provide a platform for conjugation of polyUb chains mediated by other Ub ligases.
source: These results strongly support that Rab10 is subjected to SdeA-mediated PR ubiquitination and that this modification may provide a platform of conjugation of polyUb chains to Rab10, which is expected to be mediated by other Ub ligases.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Infection with a ΔsidCΔsdcA strain still caused both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10 but with reduced levels.
source: Infection of cells with a ΔsidCΔsdcA strain as well as with a strain lacking all the SidC-family proteins (ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB) still caused both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10 but with reduced levels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Infection with the ΔsidEs strain eliminated both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10.
source: On the contrary, infection with the ΔsidEs strain eliminated both modifications.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: SidE-family proteins primarily contribute toward ubiquitination of Rab10.
source: These results support that SidE-family proteins primarily contribute toward ubiquitination of Rab10, and that SidC-family proteins partly contribute toward polyubiquitination of Rab10 directly or indirectly in conditions where Rab10 is modified with PR-Ub.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: SidC-family proteins partly contribute toward polyubiquitination of Rab10 in conditions where Rab10 is modified with PR-Ub.
source: These results support that SidE-family proteins primarily contribute toward ubiquitination of Rab10, and that SidC-family proteins partly contribute toward polyubiquitination of Rab10 directly or indirectly in conditions where Rab10 is modified with PR-Ub.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Substitution of Lys102, Lys136, and Lys154 of Rab10 to Ala did not abolish polyubiquitination of Rab10.
source: We also found that substitution of three residues on Rab10 (Lys102, Lys136, and Lys154) that were previously suggested to be potential ubiquitination sites (Jeng et al., 2019) to Ala (Rab10KKK) did not abolish polyubiquitination of Rab10 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), implying that ubiquitination sites can be present in the other residues.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Ubiquitination sites on Rab10 can be present in residues other than Lys102, Lys136, and Lys154.
source: We also found that substitution of three residues on Rab10 (Lys102, Lys136, and Lys154) that were previously suggested to be potential ubiquitination sites (Jeng et al., 2019) to Ala (Rab10KKK) did not abolish polyubiquitination of Rab10 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), implying that ubiquitination sites can be present in the other residues.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Canonical Ub chains can be formed partly on PR-Ub conjugated to Rab10.
source: This raises the possibility that canonical Ub chains can be formed partly on PR-Ub conjugated to Rab10.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The polyubiquitination of Rab10 was significantly observed until 7 hr after infection.
source: The polyubiquitination of Rab10 was significantly observed until 7 hr after infection, although the level was slightly reduced (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Rab10 ubiquitination is highly correlated with its localization to the LCV.
source: Earlier studies demonstrated that Rab10 ubiquitination is highly correlated with its localization to the LCV (Jeng et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Infection with the ΔsidEs strain drastically reduced the level of Rab10-positive LCVs at all time points examined.
source: Infection with the ΔsidEs strain drastically reduced the level of Rab10-positive LCVs at all time points examined (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: PR ubiquitination is required for Rab10 to localize to the LCV.
source: As reported for Rab33b (Kawabata et al., 2021), PR ubiquitination is thought to be required for Rab10 to localize to the LCV.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 2b and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The ΔsidCΔsdcA LCV exhibited a reduced level of Rab10 localization at 1 hr after infection.
source: The ΔsidCΔsdcA LCV also exhibited a reduced the level of Rab10 localization at 1 hr after infection (Figure 2b, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The level of Rab10 recruitment to the ΔsidCΔsdcA LCV recovered at 4 hr after infection.
source: However, the level of Rab10 recruitment to the ΔsidCΔsdcA LCV recovered at 4 hr after infection, while that to the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB LCV did not recover even as late as 7 hr (Figure 2b, middle and right panels).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The level of Rab10 recruitment to the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB LCV did not recover even as late as 7 hr after infection.
source: However, the level of Rab10 recruitment to the ΔsidCΔsdcA LCV recovered at 4 hr after infection, while that to the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB LCV did not recover even as late as 7 hr (Figure 2b, middle and right panels).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: SdcB can contribute toward retention of Rab10 on the LCV at late stages of infection.
source: This result suggests that SdcB can contribute toward retention of Rab10 on the LCV at late stages of infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Ub accumulation on the LCV has been thought to be mediated largely by SidC and SdcA.
source: The Ub accumulation on the LCV has been thought to be mediated largely by SidC and SdcA (Horenkamp et al., 2014; Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SdcB was detected around the LCV at 1 hr after infection.
source: When HeLa-FcγRII cells were infected with these strains for 1 hr, SdcB was detected around the LCV (Figure 3a, b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: The level of wild-type SdcB-positive LCVs was relatively lower compared with that of the SdcBC57A-positive LCVs at 1 hr after infection.
source: The level of wild-type SdcB-positive LCVs was relatively lower compared with that of the SdcBC57A-positive LCVs, probably due to its catalytic cycling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b and includes a speculative explanation.

claim: Expression of wild-type SdcB led to recruitment of Ub to the vacuole even without SidC and SdcA.
source: The expression of wild-type SdcB led to recruitment of Ub to the vacuole even without SidC and SdcA, while expression of SdcBC57A did not (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: SdcB has a catalytic activity to conjugate Ub to substrates on the LCV.
source: This result indicates that SdcB has a catalytic activity to conjugate Ub to substrates on the LCV.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: At 7 hr after infection, the level of the SdcB-positive LCVs was elevated to about 70% regardless of its catalytic activity.
source: At 7 hr after infection, the level of the SdcB-positive LCVs was elevated to about 70% regardless of its catalytic activity (Figure 3c, d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c and 3d.

claim: At 7 hr after infection, the level of the Ub-positive LCVs was raised to about 60%, but only when SdcB was catalytically active.
source: At this time point, the level of the Ub-positive LCVs was also raised to about 60 %, but only when SdcB was catalytically active.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: SdcB can play a substantial role to conjugate Ub to substrates on the LCV at late stages of infection.
source: These results demonstrate that SdcB can play a substantial role to conjugate Ub to substrates on the LCV at late stages of infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A substantial amount of ubiquitinated Rab10QL, but not Rab10TN, was detected upon infection with the wild-type strain.
source: A substantial amount of ubiquitinated Rab10QL, but not Rab10TN, was detected upon infection with the wild-type strain (Figure 4a; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ubiquitination of Rab10TN detected with HA-probing was apparently indirect and not infection-induced.
source: We found that ubiquitination of Rab10TN detected with HA-probing (HA-Ub) was apparently indirect and not infection-induced, as FLAG-probing (FLAG-Rab10) mostly eliminated the high molecular weight smears on Rab10TN (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Polyubiquitinated Rab10QL was reduced by infection with the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB strain.
source: Polyubiquitinated Rab10QL was reduced by infection with the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB strain, while both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10QL was mostly blocked by infection with the ΔsidEs strain.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10QL was mostly blocked by infection with the ΔsidEs strain.
source: Polyubiquitinated Rab10QL was reduced by infection with the ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB strain, while both mono- and polyubiquitination of Rab10QL was mostly blocked by infection with the ΔsidEs strain.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Localization of active Rab10 (Rab10QL) on the LCVs was apparently correlated with the level of its polyubiquitination.
source: Localization of active Rab10 (Rab10QL) on the LCVs was apparently correlated with the level of its polyubiquitination (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The active form of Rab10 is preferentially targeted and spatially regulated by the action of SidE- and SidC-family ligases.
source: The finding that the active form of Rab10 is preferentially targeted and spatially regulated by the action of SidE- and SidC-family ligases prompted us to examine the effect of SdcB activity on ubiquitination of this specific form of Rab10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4a and 4b.

claim: Bacterially expressed SdcB, but not its catalytic mutant, significantly enhanced the level of polyubiquitination of Rab10QL at 7 hr after infection.
source: Bacterially expressed SdcB, but not its catalytic mutant, significantly enhanced the level of polyubiquitination of Rab10QL at 7 hr after infection (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: At 7 hr post infection, Rab10 localization was readily detected on ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB LCVs containing wild-type SdcB, but not the inactive SdcBC57A mutant.
source: At 7 hr post infection, Rab10 localization was readily detected on ΔsidCΔsdcAΔsdcB LCVs containing wild-type SdcB, but not the inactive SdcBC57A mutant (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher with expression of wild-type SdcB than that of the catalytic mutant.
source: The level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher with expression of wild-type SdcB than that of the catalytic mutant (Figure 4e), suggesting that the Ub ligation activity of SdcB supports retention of Rab10 on the LCV until late stages of infection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The Ub ligation activity of SdcB supports retention of Rab10 on the LCV until late stages of infection.
source: The level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher with expression of wild-type SdcB than that of the catalytic mutant (Figure 4e), suggesting that the Ub ligation activity of SdcB supports retention of Rab10 on the LCV until late stages of infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: A potential relationship between SdcB and MavC as an effector/metaeffector pair was suggested by a systematic analysis utilizing yeast genetics.
source: A potential relationship between SdcB and MavC as an effector/metaeffector pair was suggested by a recent systematic analysis utilizing yeast genetics (Urbanus et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T-FcγRII cells, 3xFLAG-tagged SdcB could not be detected.
source: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T-FcγRII cells, 3xFLAG-tagged SdcB could not be detected (Figure 5a, top panel, most left lane).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Coexpression of GFP-tagged MavC, but not of its catalytic mutant, recovered the detection of SdcB.
source: However, we found that coexpression of GFP-tagged MavC, but not of its catalytic mutant (MavCC74A), recovered the detection of SdcB (Figure 5a, top panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: SdcB may be chemically modified by MavC and the modification may result in enhanced detection of this protein.
source: As SdcB was resolved as a doublet in the immunoblot, we suspected that SdcB may be chemically modified by MavC and that the modification may result in enhanced detection of this protein.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Ub was conjugated to SdcB by MavC.
source: The upper band was stained with anti-HA antibody, showing that Ub was conjugated to SdcB presumably by the known Ub conjugation ability of MavC (Gan et al., 2019a; Figure 5a, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a and a citation to previous literature.

claim: The disappearance of the SdcB bands correlated with the appearance of the high molecular weight smears when probed with anti-HA antibody.
source: We also found that the disappearance of the SdcB bands correlated with the appearance of the high molecular weight smears when probed with anti-HA antibody (Figure 5a, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The disappearance of the SdcB band can be caused by auto-ubiquitination.
source: This suggests that the disappearance of the SdcB band can be caused by auto-ubiquitination, as SdcB has an ability to catalyze auto-ubiquitination with a diverse repertoire of E2 enzymes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) consistently with a previous report (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5a and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SdcB has an ability to catalyze auto-ubiquitination with a diverse repertoire of E2 enzymes.
source: This suggests that the disappearance of the SdcB band can be caused by auto-ubiquitination, as SdcB has an ability to catalyze auto-ubiquitination with a diverse repertoire of E2 enzymes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) consistently with a previous report (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and a citation to previous literature.

claim: MG132 treatment of the cells did not rescue the disappearance of the SdcB bands.
source: A proteasome inhibitor MG132 treatment of the cells did not rescue the disappearance of the SdcB bands, suggesting that auto-ubiquitinated SdcB was not subjected to proteasomal degradation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a), but the auto-ubiquitination rather caused its apparent loss by the band distribution on the gel.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Auto-ubiquitinated SdcB was not subjected to proteasomal degradation.
source: A proteasome inhibitor MG132 treatment of the cells did not rescue the disappearance of the SdcB bands, suggesting that auto-ubiquitinated SdcB was not subjected to proteasomal degradation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a), but the auto-ubiquitination rather caused its apparent loss by the band distribution on the gel.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2a.

claim: The auto-ubiquitination of SdcB caused its apparent loss by the band distribution on the gel.
source: A proteasome inhibitor MG132 treatment of the cells did not rescue the disappearance of the SdcB bands, suggesting that auto-ubiquitinated SdcB was not subjected to proteasomal degradation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a), but the auto-ubiquitination rather caused its apparent loss by the band distribution on the gel.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2a.

claim: The catalytic activity-dependent reduction of apparent SdcB level was also detected in infected cells.
source: The catalytic activity-dependent reduction of apparent SdcB level was also detected in infected cells (Figure 4c, bottom panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The transglutaminase activity of MavC is likely required for conjugation of Ub to SdcB.
source: The transglutaminase activity of MavC is likely required for conjugation of Ub to SdcB, as the catalytic mutant of MavC (MavC C74A) failed to modify SdcB (Figure 5a).

claim: Unmodified SdcB was readily detected when the SdcB C57 active site was mutated regardless of the presence of MavC.

evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcBC57A was not readily detected.
source: Interestingly, the MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcBC57A was not readily detected (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The catalytic residue C57 of SdcB is crucial in being modified by MavC.
source: This indicates that the catalytic residue C57 of SdcB is crucial in being modified by MavC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: MavC suppresses the E3 ligase activity of SdcB by the unique chemical modification.
source: As suggested by the reduction of the high molecular weight smears (Figure 5a), it is plausible that MavC suppresses the E3 ligase activity of SdcB by the unique chemical modification.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: In the presence of MavC, but not of its paralog MvcA, the mass shift of SdcB was readily detected in vitro.
source: In the presence of MavC, but not of its paralog MvcA, the mass shift of SdcB was readily detected (Figure 5c, top panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The shifted band of SdcB contains Ub.
source: The immunoblotting showed that the band contains Ub (Figure 5C, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The presence of wild-type MavC, but not its catalytic mutant, reduced SdcB auto-ubiquitination in vitro.
source: The presence of wild-type MavC, but not its catalytic mutant, also reduced SdcB auto-ubiquitination in vitro (Figure 5—figure supplement 2b).

claim: Ub was conjugated to SdcA but not to SidC by the catalytic activity of MavC.
source: These results clearly demonstrated that Ub was conjugated to SdcA but not to SidC by the catalytic activity of MavC, and that this modification occurred only to SdcA in the catalytically active form.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: MavC-mediated Ub modification of SdcA occurred only to SdcA in the catalytically active form.
source: These results clearly demonstrated that Ub was conjugated to SdcA but not to SidC by the catalytic activity of MavC, and that this modification occurred only to SdcA in the catalytically active form.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The use of Ub having no Lys residues resulted in an enhanced level of Ub conjugation to SdcB mediated by functional MavC.
source: The use of Ub having no Lys residues (HA-Ub No K) resulted in an enhanced level of Ub conjugation to SdcB mediated by functional MavC (Figure 5e, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: HA-UbAA did not conjugate to SdcB.
source: Surprisingly, HA-UbAA did not conjugate to SdcB, indicating that the C-terminal Gly-Gly residues are essential for MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcB (Figure 5f, second panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The C-terminal Gly-Gly residues are essential for MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcB.
source: Surprisingly, HA-UbAA did not conjugate to SdcB, indicating that the C-terminal Gly-Gly residues are essential for MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcB (Figure 5f, second panel).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The shifted band detected by FLAG probing represents conjugation of cellular intrinsic Ub.
source: The shifted band detected by FLAG probing represents conjugation of cellular intrinsic Ub (Figure 5f, top panel) as probed by Ub antibody (Figure 5f, third panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Transglutaminase activity of MavC targets Gln40 of Ub to catalyze intramolecular crosslinking.
source: Transglutaminase activity of MavC is known to target Gln40 of Ub to catalyze the intramolecular crosslinking (Gan et al., 2019a; Guan et al., 2020; Puvar et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A covalent bond was formed between Gln41 of Ub and Lys518 of SdcB.
source: We found that a covalent bond was formed between Gln41 of Ub and Lys518 of SdcB (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometric analysis data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Crosslinking between Gln31 of Ub and Lys891 of SdcB was also detected.
source: Crosslinking between Gln31 of Ub and Lys891 of SdcB was also detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometric analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ub Q41E failed to be conjugated to SdcB.
source: Consistent with the result from the MS analysis, Ub Q41E, but not Ub Q40E, failed to be conjugated to SdcB, showing that Gln41 is crucial for MavC-mediated crosslinking with SdcB (Figure 6b, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Gln41 is crucial for MavC-mediated crosslinking with SdcB.
source: Consistent with the result from the MS analysis, Ub Q41E, but not Ub Q40E, failed to be conjugated to SdcB, showing that Gln41 is crucial for MavC-mediated crosslinking with SdcB (Figure 6b, middle panel).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Ub Q31E also reduced the level of modified SdcB.
source: Ub Q31E also reduced the level of modified SdcB, and Ub Q31E Q41E completely abolished the crosslinking to SdcB.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Ub Q31E Q41E completely abolished the crosslinking to SdcB.
source: Ub Q31E also reduced the level of modified SdcB, and Ub Q31E Q41E completely abolished the crosslinking to SdcB.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The presence of modified SdcB bands when probed with anti-FLAG antibody is caused by conjugation with intrinsic Ub in cells.
source: The presence of modified SdcB bands when probed with anti-FLAG antibody is thought to be caused by conjugation with intrinsic Ub in cells (Figure 6b, top panel).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Replacement of Lys518 and Lys891 of SdcB to Arg showed lesser impact on abolishing the reactivity with MavC.
source: Contrarily, replacement of Lys518 and Lys891 of SdcB to Arg (SdcB K518R, SdcB K891R, and SdcB K518R K891R), which have no apparent effect on Rab10 ubiquitination (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), showed lesser impact on abolishing the reactivity (Figure 6c), suggesting that additional residues of SdcB can be subjected to MavC-dependent Ub conjugation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: SdcB K518R K891R has no apparent effect on Rab10 ubiquitination.
source: Contrarily, replacement of Lys518 and Lys891 of SdcB to Arg (SdcB K518R, SdcB K891R, and SdcB K518R K891R), which have no apparent effect on Rab10 ubiquitination (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), showed lesser impact on abolishing the reactivity (Figure 6c), suggesting that additional residues of SdcB can be subjected to MavC-dependent Ub conjugation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Additional residues of SdcB can be subjected to MavC-dependent Ub conjugation.
source: Contrarily, replacement of Lys518 and Lys891 of SdcB to Arg (SdcB K518R, SdcB K891R, and SdcB K518R K891R), which have no apparent effect on Rab10 ubiquitination (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), showed lesser impact on abolishing the reactivity (Figure 6c), suggesting that additional residues of SdcB can be subjected to MavC-dependent Ub conjugation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Association of the C-terminal Gly of Ub to the catalytic pocket of SdcA or SdcB positions these molecules in proper orientation for intramolecular crosslinking mediated by MavC.
source: Taken together, we currently hypothesize that association of the C-terminal Gly of Ub to the catalytic pocket of SdcA or SdcB (C44 or C57, respectively) positions these molecules in proper orientation for intramolecular crosslinking mediated by the transglutaminase activity of MavC.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the experimental data.

claim: At 4 hr after infection, the level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher in cells expressing the catalytic mutant of MavC compared with those expressing wild-type MavC.
source: At 4 hr after infection with L. pneumophila strains expressing 3xFLAG-SdcB, the level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher in the cells expressing the catalytic mutant of MavC compared with those expressing wild-type MavC (Figure 7a, b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7a and 7b.

claim: Rab10 localization was reduced coincident with MavC-dependent inhibition of SdcB.
source: That Rab10 localization was reduced coincident with MavC-dependent inhibition of SdcB further supports the contribution of SdcB activity toward retention of Rab10 on the LCV.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 7a and 7b.

claim: At 9 hr after infection with the wild-type strain, the level of Rab10-positive LCVs was reduced to about 20% of the total LCVs.
source: At 9 hr after infection with the wild-type strain, the level of Rab10-positive LCVs was reduced to about 20% of the total LCVs (compare with that of 1–7 hr infection (~40%)) (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c and comparison with Figure 2b.

claim: The level of Rab10-positive LCVs was significantly higher in cells infected with a ΔmavCΔmvcA strain at 9 hr after infection.
source: However, the level got significantly higher in the cells infected with a ΔmavCΔmvcA strain.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: When cells were infected with a strain lacking Lpg2149, the level of Rab10-positive LCVs declined at 9 hr after infection.
source: Contrary, when the cells were infected with a strain lacking Lpg2149 which inhibits the activity of MavC and MvcA, the level declined.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: MavC suppresses the activity of SdcB in infection conditions and thereby downregulates Rab10 localization to the LCV at later stages of infection.
source: These results support that MavC suppresses the activity of SdcB in infection conditions and thereby downregulates Rab10 localization to the LCV at later stages of infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Rab10 localization is finely regulated during infection.
source: Taken together, we found that Rab10 localization is finely regulated during infection; the interplay of bacterial enzymes leads to sustained association of Rab10 with the LCV and eventually dissociates it from the LCV presumably in accordance with the process of the LCV biogenesis (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The interplay of bacterial enzymes leads to sustained association of Rab10 with the LCV and eventually dissociates it from the LCV.
source: Taken together, we found that Rab10 localization is finely regulated during infection; the interplay of bacterial enzymes leads to sustained association of Rab10 with the LCV and eventually dissociates it from the LCV presumably in accordance with the process of the LCV biogenesis (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Subversion of Rab1 function is critical for L. pneumophila to create the replicative vacuole.
source: Following the finding that subversion of Rab1 function is critical for L. pneumophila to create the replicative vacuole (Kagan et al., 2004), remarkable numbers of studies have revealed the molecular mechanisms of how L. pneumophila T4SS effectors modulate the localization and enzymatic activity of Rab1 (Qiu and Luo, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The importance of Rab10 and its chaperone RABIF for intracellular replication of L. pneumophila has recently emerged.
source: The importance of Rab10 and its chaperone RABIF for intracellular replication of L. pneumophila has recently emerged (Jeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Little is known about how L. pneumophila manipulates the activity of Rab10 prior to this study.
source: However, little is known about how L. pneumophila manipulates the activity of Rab10.
evidence: This statement indicates a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: PR-Ub modification of Rab10 may provide the platform for further modification of Rab10.
source: The PR-Ub modification of Rab10 and ubiquitination of unknown LCV-associated substrates of the SidC family may provide the platform for the further modification of Rab10.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Involvement of MavC for regulation of the SidC-family ligases was unexpectedly identified in this study.
source: Involvement of MavC for regulation of the SidC-family ligases was unexpectedly identified in our analyses.
evidence: This is a statement about a finding of the current study.

claim: The finding that MavC regulates SidC-family ligases has added another layer of complexity to effector-mediated regulation of Rab10.
source: This finding has added another layer of complexity to effector-mediated regulation of Rab10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the significance of the findings.

claim: The result showing that Q41 of Ub is crosslinked with SdcB gives a new insight into the molecular mechanism of how MavC catalyzes Ub conjugation to specific substrates.
source: Our result showing that Q41 of Ub is crosslinked with SdcB gives a new insight into the molecular mechanism of how MavC catalyzes Ub conjugation to specific substrates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the significance of the findings.

claim: The ability of SdcB as a Ub ligase to position a Ub molecule into its active site is a requirement for MavC to form the covalent bond between Ub and SdcB.
source: This strongly suggests that the ability of SdcB as a Ub ligase to position a Ub molecule into its active site is a requirement for MavC to form the covalent bond between Ub and SdcB.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The reaction scheme for MavC-mediated Ub conjugation to SdcB is reminiscent of how MavC mediates Ub conjugation to UBE2N.
source: This model is reminiscent of the reaction scheme described for how MavC mediates Ub conjugation to UBE2N, in which the initial capturing of Ub by the E2 activity of UBE2N allows enhanced activity by MavC (Puvar et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Suppression of SdcB activity can be beneficial for release of Rab10 at the maturation stage of LCV biogenesis.
source: We investigated SdcB in terms of the MavC-mediated regulation in this study and found that suppression of its activity can be beneficial for release of Rab10 at the maturation stage of LCV biogenesis (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 7d.

claim: MavC may have multiple targets including SdcA which can be involved in the early stage of infection.
source: However, MavC may have multiple targets including SdcA (Figure 5d) which can be involved in the early stage of infection.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: How MavC regulates the entire process of the vacuolar modification needs to be addressed in future studies.
source: How MavC regulates the entire process of the vacuolar modification needs to be addressed in future studies.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: SdcB has an ankyrin repeat (ANK) domain at its C-terminus.
source: In contrast to the PI[4]P-binding domain present in SidC and SdcA, SdcB has an ankyrin repeat (ANK) domain at its C-terminus.
evidence: This is a statement about the structural features of SdcB.

claim: ANK domains are generally known to mediate protein–protein interactions.
source: As ANK domains are generally known to mediate protein–protein interactions, we speculate that SdcB targets substrates distinct from those of SidC and SdcA.
evidence: This statement is based on general knowledge about ANK domains.

claim: SdcB targets substrates distinct from those of SidC and SdcA.
source: As ANK domains are generally known to mediate protein–protein interactions, we speculate that SdcB targets substrates distinct from those of SidC and SdcA.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural features of SdcB.

claim: The lipid-binding ability of SidC and SdcA implicates their substrate specificity.
source: The lipid-binding ability of SidC and SdcA implicates their substrate specificity; their substrates are on or associated with the LCV in the specific stages of vacuole remodeling (Vormittag et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SidC and SdcA substrates are on or associated with the LCV in specific stages of vacuole remodeling.
source: The lipid-binding ability of SidC and SdcA implicates their substrate specificity; their substrates are on or associated with the LCV in the specific stages of vacuole remodeling (Vormittag et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SdcB can target substrate(s) present on the LCV in maturation stages different from ones when SidC and SdcA can work.
source: We, therefore, speculate that SdcB can target substrate(s) present on the LCV in maturation stages different from ones when SidC and SdcA can work in.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural and functional differences between SdcB and SidC/SdcA.

claim: The authors have not succeeded to identify cellular targets with which the ANK domain of SdcB interacts.
source: In spite of our extensive efforts, we have not succeeded to identify cellular targets with which the ANK domain of SdcB interacts.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study.

claim: Identifying enzymatic substrates of SdcB would help understand its exact biological role in L. pneumophila infection.
source: It would be a future perspective to understand the exact biological role of SdcB as a Ub ligase in L. pneumophila infection by identifying its enzymatic substrates.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: L. pneumophila has a multi-tiered regulatory mechanism to manipulate Ub signaling cascades involving SidC- and SidE-family Ub ligases.
source: We found that L. pneumophila has a multi-tiered regulatory mechanism to manipulate Ub signaling cascades in which SidC- and SidE-family Ub ligases are involved, even though the exact molecular mechanism how Ub modification of Rab10 results in regulation of its LCV residency would be an open question.

source: MavC was found to contribute to fine-tuning the regulation via its unique Ub conjugation activity toward SdcB.

claim: These regulations are reflected in many aspects of the LCV biogenesis and maturation which are thought to be largely controlled by Ub signaling.
source: These regulations are reflected in many aspects of the LCV biogenesis and maturation which are thought to be largely controlled by Ub signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the broader significance of the findings.

source: The regulatory cascade of Rab10 GTPase, whose function is crucial for ER recruitment to the LCV, became apparent in this study.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the findings of the study.

claim: Similar regulatory cascades likely exist for many LCV-associated proteins.
source: Most likely, similar regulatory cascades exist for many LCV-associated proteins.
